references.text: Moses stretches out his hand over the sea, and the Lord drives back the sea with a strong east wind. This verse describes the same action of Moses' hand over the sea.
The Lord commands Moses to stretch out his hand over the sea to split it. This is the precursor to the action described in verse 27.
Moses' song describes how Pharaoh's army was cast into the sea, and his chosen commanders drowned in the Sea of Reeds.
A summary of the event where the sea returned upon the Egyptians while Israel crossed through on dry ground.
The psalm praises the Lord who shook Pharaoh and his army in the Sea of Reeds.
The psalm describes how God led the people safely forward, while the sea overwhelmed their enemies.
The water covered over their opponents; not one of them was left behind.
Joshua reminds the people how the Lord drove the sea over the Egyptians when they pursued the Israelites.
Isaiah refers to the Lord who made a way through the sea and led out chariots and horses that lay there and did not rise again.
Hebrews mentions the act of faith as the Israelites passed through the Red Sea, while the Egyptians drowned when they tried the same.
God's use of an east wind as judgment (locusts) versus salvation/judgment at the sea demonstrates God's sovereignty over the forces of nature.
Joshua confirms and summarizes the event in Exodus 14 as evidence of God's action against Egypt.
13:18 explains God's strategic leadership that led the people to the sea where the miracle in 14:27 could take place.
